concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 15 September 2026
justifications: On 15 September 2026, the amendment reducing the deadline had been signed but was not yet effective. The DPA therefore required notification no later than 48 hours after awareness of a breach.

concepts.name: Breach notification deadline in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment was effective from 1 October 2026 and replaced the 48-hour deadline with a requirement to notify the Controller no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a breach.

concepts.name: Audit notice period in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: The amendment reduced the routine on-site audit notice period to 20 days. The 10-business-day period in the audit protocol is in an annex, which is subordinate to the amendment's main body.

concepts.name: Liability cap in force on 1 November 2026
justifications: As in force on 1 November 2026, the amendment set the Processor's aggregate liability cap at EUR 1,000,000, irrespective of the EUR 700,000 in fees paid.

concepts.name: Liability cap covers confidentiality breaches
justifications: The amendment expressly provides that the EUR 1,000,000 liability cap does not apply to breaches of the confidentiality obligations.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 November 2026
justifications: Meridian Mail Ltd remained an approved Sub-processor on 1 November 2026; its approval was not withdrawn until 1 January 2027.

concepts.name: Meridian Mail approved on 1 February 2027
justifications: The approval of Meridian Mail Ltd was withdrawn effective 1 January 2027, so it was not an approved Sub-processor on 1 February 2027.

concepts.name: Distinct data locations count as of 1 February 2027
justifications: As of 1 February 2027, the distinct data-location countries were Norway, Estonia, Lithuania, France, and Denmark.

concepts.name: Deletion deadline for year-end termination
justifications: The amendment effective on 1 October 2026 reduced the deletion or return period from 90 to 60 days. A termination on 31 December 2026 therefore gives a latest deadline of 1 March 2027.

concepts.name: Breach notification obligation summary
predicted: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach. the notification must include key details such as the breach's nature, affected data subjects and records, likely consequences, and mitigation measures.
gold: the processor must notify the controller without undue delay and within 24 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting data processed under the dpa, describing its nature, affected categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and records, likely consequences, and measures taken or proposed to address the breach and mitigate its effects. it must document all breaches and cooperate with any regulatory notifications or data subject communications the controller determines are required.
values: The Processor must notify the Controller without undue delay and no later than 24 hours after becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach. The notification must include key details such as the breach's nature, affected data subjects and records, likely consequences, and mitigation measures.
justifications: This reflects the amended 24-hour notification deadline and the continuing notification-content requirements in force on 1 November 2026.

concepts.name: Applicable initial notification regime
justifications: The incident involved confirmed exposure of usable privileged credentials, which triggers the expedited initial-notification regime with a 12-hour outer limit.

concepts.name: Initial notice lateness in minutes
justifications: Awareness occurred at 17:10 on 9 April, making the 12-hour outer limit 05:10 on 10 April. The first notice arrived at 06:00, exceeding the limit by 50 minutes.

concepts.name: Completed follow-up report deadline
justifications: The third Business Day after awareness is 16 April: 12 April is a contractual closure date, 14 April is an approved pause day, and the deadline falls at the end of the third counted Business Day.

concepts.name: Held ORD records deletion deadline
justifications: The ordinary deletion deadline is 60 calendar days after termination on 30 June, resulting in 29 August. Because the final hold ends on 25 August, the records must instead be deleted after the later tenth Business Day deadline, which falls on 9 September.

concepts.name: BK-0630 deletion deadline
justifications: The backup contains no held records, so it is subject to the earlier of its ordinary deletion deadline and 35 calendar days after creation. Thirty-five days after creation on 30 June is 4 August, earlier than the 60-day ordinary deadline.

concepts.name: Permitted uses of held ORD records on 1 September 2027
justifications: After termination, records retained solely under a legal hold may be used only for legal preservation. The requested analytics use was rejected, and service delivery and analytics are expressly prohibited.

concepts.name: Nordlicht infrastructure approval start
justifications: Approval for the Stockholm infrastructure service could begin only after the proposed start date, written consent, and completed security review. The security review and actual processing began on 22 April 2027, the latest applicable condition.

concepts.name: Ordinary customer email providers on 10 May 2027
justifications: Cendrillon Mail SAS continues ordinary transactional email from France. Meridian Mail Ltd was not authorised for ordinary customer transactional email during the queried period because its emergency permission did not reinstate that authorisation.

concepts.name: Authorised data locations on 15 May 2027
justifications: On 15 May 2027, processing and effective authorisation are established for storage in Norway, facilities in Estonia and Lithuania, ordinary transactional email in France, and Nordlicht's Stockholm infrastructure service in Sweden. Denmark had ceased processing after withdrawal, while Finland and Germany lacked the required conditions.

concepts.name: Written consent date for Nordlicht email in Finland
Security cap before earlier payments in EUR
justifications: Qualifying fees are EUR 1,440,000 excluding 20% VAT, less the EUR 60,000 service credit, resulting in EUR 1,140,000. Twice that amount is EUR 2,280,000, which exceeds the EUR 2,000,000 minimum security cap.

concepts.name: Ordinary cap remaining before new claims in EUR
justifications: The EUR 1,000,000 ordinary cap is reduced by EUR 300,000 in earlier ordinary-breach payments, leaving EUR 700,000 before the new claims.

concepts.name: Total payable on new claims in EUR
justifications: The ordinary claim pays EUR 700,000 after its remaining-pool limit; the shared security loss pays EUR 1,750,000; and the two confidentiality-priority losses pay EUR 250,000 and EUR 100,000 uncapped. The duplicate security claims for the same loss are counted only once.
